Let the given matrix be $A$:
$$A = \begin{pmatrix}
 \frac{4}{3} & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} & -\frac{13}{3} \\
 -\frac{13}{3} & \frac{25}{6} & -\frac{19}{6} & \frac{11}{6} \\
 -\frac{23}{6} & \frac{29}{6} & -\frac{10}{3} & -\frac{19}{6} \\
 -\frac{17}{6} & -\frac{7}{6} & \frac{5}{2} & \frac{7}{3} \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
We can multiply the entire matrix by the least common multiple of the denominators, which is 6. This will multiply the determinant by $6^4 = 1296$.
$$6A = \begin{pmatrix}
 8 & 6 & -27 & -26 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\
 -23 & 29 & -20 & -19 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
Now we compute the determinant of $6A$.
Let $R_i$ denote the $i$-th row.
$R_1 \leftarrow R_1 + R_4$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 & -12 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\
 -23 & 29 & -20 & -19 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - R_2$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 & -12 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\
 3 & 4 & -1 & -30 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 2R_3$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 & -12 \\
 -32 & 17 & -17 & 71 \\
 3 & 4 & -1 & -30 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$C_3 \leftarrow C_3 - 12C_2$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & 0 & -12 \\
 -32 & 17 & -221 & 71 \\
 3 & 4 & -49 & -30 \\
 -17 & -7 & 99 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$C_4 \leftarrow C_4 - 12C_2$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\
 -32 & 17 & -221 & -133 \\
 3 & 4 & -49 & -78 \\
 -17 & -7 & 99 & 98 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
Expand along the first row:
$$(-1) \cdot (-1)^{1+2} \begin{vmatrix}
 -32 & -221 & -133 \\
 3 & -49 & -78 \\
 -17 & 99 & 98 \\
\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}
 -32 & -221 & -133 \\
 3 & -49 & -78 \\
 -17 & 99 & 98 \\
\end{vmatrix}$$
Multiply the first column by 2.
$2 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}
 -32 & -221 & -133 \\
 3 & -49 & -78 \\
 -17 & 99 & 98 \\
\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}
 -64 & -221 & -133 \\
 6 & -49 & -78 \\
 -34 & 99 & 98 \\
\end{vmatrix}$
This path is becoming complicated. Let's restart from $6A$.

Let's use row operations to make more zeros.
$$6A = \begin{pmatrix}
 8 & 6 & -27 & -26 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\
 -23 & 29 & -20 & -19 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$R_1 \leftarrow R_1 + R_4$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 & -12 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\
 -23 & 29 & -20 & -19 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$C_4 \leftarrow C_4 - C_3$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 & 0 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 30 \\
 -23 & 29 & -20 & 1 \\
 -17 & -7 & 15 & -1 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
$R_4 \leftarrow R_4 + R_3$:
$$ \begin{pmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 & 0 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 & 30 \\
 -23 & 29 & -20 & 1 \\
 -40 & 22 & -5 & 0 \\
\end{pmatrix}$$
Now expand along the 4th column:
$$ \det(6A) = -1 \cdot (-1)^{3+4} \begin{vmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 \\
 -40 & 22 & -5 \\
\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}
 -9 & -1 & -12 \\
 -26 & 25 & -19 \\
 -40 & 22 & -5 \\
\end{vmatrix}$$
$$ = -9(25 \cdot -5 - (-19) \cdot 22) - (-1)(-26 \cdot -5 - (-19) \cdot -40) + (-12)(-26 \cdot 22 - 25 \cdot -40)$$
$$ = -9(-125 + 418) + (130 - 760) - 12(-572 + 1000)$$
$$ = -9(293) - 630 - 12(428)$$
$$ = -2637 - 630 - 5136$$
$$ = -8403$$
So, $\det(6A) = -8403$.
Therefore, $\det(A) = \frac{-8403}{6^4} = \frac{-8403}{1296}$.
We can simplify the fraction. The sum of digits of 8403 is 15, so it is divisible by 3. $8403 = 3 \cdot 2801$.
The sum of digits of 1296 is 18, so it is divisible by 3 and 9. $1296 = 3 \cdot 432$.
Thus, $\det(A) = \frac{-2801}{432}$.

The final answer is $\boxed{-\frac{2801}{432}}$.
